newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea blasts Japan PM on war apology.
newsitem.headline: North Korea blasts Japan PM on war apology.

text.p: North Korea's state-run media on Monday criticised Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's apology for Japan's actions during World War Two.

"The attitude of the Japanese authorities on one hand to string vague words without a true sense of atonement...and on the other hand allowing cabinet ministers to visit the Yasukuni Shrine...represents a farce," Korean Central Radio said in a broadcast monitored by Japan's Radiopress news agency.

In a speech at a war memorial ceremony in Tokyo last Friday, Hashimoto said: "The last war caused tremendous pain and sorrow not only to our country but also to people in many countries, particularly those in neighbouring Asian nations."

The North Korean radio said Japan's revisionist moves reached a climax on Friday when a number of cabinet ministers visited Yasukuni Shrine, a controversial war shrine housing the spirits of Japan's 2.6 million war dead, including Class-A war criminals.
Such a performance, the North Korean radio said, was aimed at promoting militarism and building a psychological foundation for future Japanese aggression.

"They encourage people with such ambitions to carry on more and more, and all the while Japan claims 'We are reflecting on past crimes', it merely uses these as a cunning trick to deceive the world," the North Korean radio said.
